No title changed. Removed or reworded original passages: six-months the ~1,500 km sentence (kept as owner guidance, reworded) and the long-term habits list (support channel wording); three-month the negotiation heading sentence (folded into the terms table); returning ten minutes, nobody charges for dust, deposit back on the spot in cash, worth their two minutes, shops are reasonable about extensions, photos-fuel-handshake-cash (all unsourced or implied policy); year expect several visits (now "may include"), still wins for most expats (now "can suit"), the relationship paragraph (reworded); inspection-checklist thirty seconds, 2-3 cm chain play and fixed in minutes (unsourced), "number plates" (a motorbike carries one rear plate, Circular 79/2024), registration certificate with the bike and insurance certificate available (now questions), "no plates", sign-photograph-ride (photos come first); common-problems same five problems, keep the contract until the cash is back, stolen from sidewalks not guarded parking, pay for attended parking (absolute claims), registration certificate at the shop and take it with the bike (now a question); what-is-included honestly split, papers and third-party insurance ride with the bike, ask to see both, helmets at most shops (no helmet policy in OWNER-FACTS), third-party cover wording (now the owner's legal duty, within its limits and conditions), agreed fuel level (fuel conventions differ), the breakdown division sentence, the closing core-and-edges line; English teachers how most teachers start, typically two to four locations, automatic scooters dominate, maintenance included (now may include, as OWNER-FACTS words it); international students none removed (100% kept): corrective sentences follow the unsourced below-ownership-cost line, the keep-the-receipt line, the loose 50cc-class wording (moped definition from Law 36/2024/QH15 Article 34(1)(g)) and the Ninh Binh weekend line (support is primarily Hanoi and local). batches.notes: Priority A choosing and riding pages (renting versus buying, scooter versus semi-automatic, parking, and the best-bike pages for commuting, tall riders, English teachers, day trips, Hanoi traffic, long distance and students), fourth batch. Every article passed an independent verifier; renting-vs-buying, scooter-vs-semi, where-to-park, commuting, tall riders, English teachers, day trips, Hanoi traffic, long distance and students each needed a fix round and passed a delta verification; the delta MINOR findings were applied by the lead with the verifier's wording and checked by lint and QA. Rules applied from writing-guide section 10: Law 36/2024/QH15 Article 56 (the rider carries the registration certificate itself, a certified copy only for a mortgaged vehicle with the bank's confirmation, the owner's compulsory insurance certificate, an electronic identification account under 56(3)); moped definition Article 34(1)(g) with age 16 under 59(1)(a); Circular 12/2025/TT-BCA Article 24(5)(a) for exchanged licences; Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT Article 6 for speed defaults (read 2026-10-25). Business limit: support is primarily for Hanoi and local use, so the day-trip and long-distance pages ask the shop before booking and imply no rescue, delivery, one-way rental or touring package. Recorded front matter changes: scooter-vs-semi description dropped "narrower, cheaper and fixable anywhere" (the widths and day rates refute it); where-to-park description dropped "typical fees" and "towing" (unsupported); tall-riders description dropped "longer seat and floor space" and "suits them best" (unsupported; the Air Blade 125 is shorter than the Vision); long-distance description dropped "rent the biggest bike your licence covers" and "full maintenance" (contradicted by the page and OWNER-FACTS) and now carries its primary keyword. No title changed. Removed or reworded original passages: renting-vs-buying purchase prices, used-bike prices and the 8-12 month break-even (unsourced, self-contradictory; replaced by a formula with no figures), the foreigner-registration and fine-band sentences (unsourced), insurance as the shop's problem (against OWNER-FACTS); scooter-vs-semi wider than an underbone, narrowest and lightest, lowest cost, thirty seconds (refuted by the widths and rates); where-to-park a few thousand dong per session, tolerated on most streets, red-and-white curbs, the riding-a-few-metres exception, towed or ticketed, most street lots close in the evening, prevents most losses (unsourced); commuting the serviceability bullet (now may include), commute standard and Ring Road (unsourced; the price figures in that sentence are kept verbatim), a hundred times a day; tall riders the low-180s height match; English teachers running costs trivial, any shop services them, exchange takes some weeks, one deposit for the term, parked all day, the break-even line, contract season; Hanoi traffic rarely clears 40 km/h, the licence-free 50 cc or e-bike item (now the moped definition); long distance highways flow at 50-80 km/h, every town can fix a Wave, fixable anywhere, the A1 sentence (now new A1 to 125 cc with the Article 89 transitional scope), agree in writing (now a question); students cheapest full motorbikes and roomier (the day rates are shared), fuel a rounding error, a few thousand dong parking, the fine costs more than a semester, the most opportunistic theft, students rent in waves; day trips none (100% kept). Price rule: existing sentences that carry a monthly figure (commuting) or the E-Bike day rate (students) keep those figures verbatim; no new weekly, monthly, 50cc or E-Bike figure was written (docs/seo/price-reconciliation.md). Source reads used Tavily extract (Firecrawl had no credits).

batches.notes: Priority A rental problem and audience pages (lost key, puncture, loose chain, outside repairs, high mileage, fuel policy, easiest and lightest bikes for beginners, digital nomads, female riders), fifth batch. Every article passed an independent verifier; lost-key passed after a fix round; punctured-tyre, easiest-beginners, lightest, loose-chain, outside-repair, high-mileage, fuel-policy and digital-nomads needed a fix round and passed a delta verification; female-riders passed on the first verification; the delta and verifier MINOR findings were applied with the verifiers' wording and checked by lint and QA. Rules applied: writing-guide section 10 (Law 36/2024/QH15 Articles 33, 34(1)(g), 56, 57, 59; Circular 12/2025/TT-BCA Article 24(5)(a)); OWNER-FACTS wording for maintenance (may include an oil change, chain adjustment and tension, tyre-pressure checks and normal inspection), consumables (may be the renter's responsibility), the ~1,500 km owner guidance and Hanoi/local support; no shop rule is implied for fuel, lost keys, outside repairs, helmets or records (all written as handover questions). Manufacturer figures only from docs/MODEL-DATABASE.md or Honda Vietnam owner's manuals read 2026-10-25 via TinyFish (Firecrawl had no credits). Recorded front matter changes and removed or reworded original passages: lost-key: description dropped "a replacement fee from your deposit, a wait while it is cut" (OWNER-FACTS publishes no lost-key charge or deposit deduction; now asks the shop what a replacement costs and how long it takes). Removed or reworded: a solvable problem with a known cost, many rental shops hold a spare, the replacement key cost paragraph, the cost settles against the deposit, agreed-charge item, the closing line (all unsourced or implied policy); Vision smart-key claim cut; Air Blade 160 smart key per docs/MODEL-DATABASE.md. punctured-tyre: description "typically the renter's consumable" became "may be the renter's consumable, so ask first" (OWNER-FACTS wording: may be the renter's responsibility depending on the situation). Removed or reworded: most common rental-bike event after refuelling, the road-debris rule stated as typical, tens of thousands of dong, paid in cash and not worth a negotiation, any tyre shop fixes it in minutes and they are everywhere (unsourced); the shop keeping condition records is a question; Yamaha publishes tyre type for two models, Honda sizes only. easiest-beginners: no front matter text change. Removed or reworded: top every list, low narrow seats and seat height kills it, small forgiving wheels, the roughly 100 kg class (now Honda's published 97 kg Vision and 96 kg Wave Alpha 110 figures), licence-free e-bike as the easiest machine (now Law 36/2024/QH15 Article 34 groups: pedal-assist bicycle and moped 50 cc / 4 kW / 50 km/h), thirty minutes in a parking lot, confidence on day two; Air Blade 160 needs class A on a new licence (Article 89 keeps older A1 below 175 cc). lightest: description dropped "Weight is what makes a new rider drop a bike" and "the lightest legal rental options" (unsourced cause; now names the published weights). Removed or reworded: nearly always the bike fell over, removes the single most common failure, both the light option and the legal one (no e-bike weight is published: "lightest class on the list" kept verbatim with its day rate under price-reconciliation rule 2 and qualified as a general description), the light mainstream motorbikes sentence (the daily figures are reworded into the table), the Latte 125 and kerb-weight-table pointer, availability moves fastest; unverified Sirius FI 98 kg and Wave Alpha versions cut. loose-chain: description dropped "a five-minute adjustment at the shop" (unsourced). Removed or reworded: the most common mechanical complaint, 2-3 cm of play (now the Honda Vietnam owner's manual figures: Wave Alpha 25-35 mm and manual 32K57A100 for models AFS110MS/MD/MCS 30-40 mm, do not ride beyond 50 mm, read 2026-10-25), five minutes, explicitly the owner's maintenance (now OWNER-FACTS: maintenance may include chain adjustment and tension), the third-party sentence (now points to the outside-repair rules), any roadside mechanic for a small cash fee. outside-repair: no front matter text change. Removed or reworded: nine times out of ten, the shop's advice is free, puzzles are decided against the renter by default, the long-distance pointer, report at return (now the same day as well as at return); maintenance wording now "may all be part of that"; the yes-list heading now says confirm by phone first. high-mileage: no front matter text change. Removed or reworded: owner guidance from experience (now OWNER-FACTS: periodic checks around every ~1,500 km of use, not a manufacturer interval), a bike that changes hands every few weeks (now a rental bike), the shop's maintenance list with brake pads and cables (now the OWNER-FACTS may-include list), the 110-125 cc wear prediction (now: what has worn depends on the bike, the load, the roads and the rider), maintenance is the shop's side of the deal (now may be), the commute article's monthly-rate arithmetic (that article has none; now the commuter's side of a monthly rental), no charge for the shop's own maintenance items (not in OWNER-FACTS; now confirm which apply). fuel-policy: description dropped "usually near-empty" and "Petrol is cheap and stations are everywhere" (unsourced market norm implying a shop rule; OWNER-FACTS states no fuel rule). Removed or reworded: fuel is always the renter's (twice), most Hanoi rentals hand over a small noted amount (now one convention you may be offered), petrol costs and the fill-from-empty figure (unsourced), the far-provinces line, RON 92 as the standard grade and not fussy (now the Honda Wave Alpha owner's manual: RON 91 or higher for the Vietnam type, ethanol 10% or less, fill to the lower edge of the filler neck, read 2026-10-25), no shop refunds the petrol left (implied policy; now a question); the range figures are stated calculations from published tank and consumption figures. female-riders: no front matter text change. Removed or reworded: thousands of women, one of the most gender-equal motorbike cities, slow average speeds (unsourced statistics and ranking), confidence machines for all riders (now the class the beginner guide puts first), helmet included with most rentals (not in OWNER-FACTS; now a handover question; the helmet duty is Law 36/2024/QH15 Article 33), only while parked (ambiguous; now the compartment while riding), the one-minute demo (invented duration), the realistic-picture close (unsourced claims about attendants and shops); bag-snatching is now quoted from the UK FCDO Vietnam travel advice (read 2026-10-25), its on-foot advice marked as such. digital-nomads: no front matter text change. Removed or reworded: better than any other transport (unsupported superlative), maintenance included on Nguyen Tu rentals (now OWNER-FACTS: may include; consumables may be the renter's), under-seat compartments hold a backpack (now a handover check), attended lots at coworking spaces and malls (unsourced), a Saturday away and the best part of the weekend (support is primarily for Hanoi and local use, so trips are agreed with the shop first); the existing Click/Mio and Vision monthly figures are kept verbatim (price-reconciliation rule 2, DIFFERENT cell, owner review). No title changed. Price rule: no new weekly, monthly, 50cc or E-Bike figure; existing sentences with such figures (lightest E-Bike day rate, digital-nomads monthly figures) are kept verbatim (docs/seo/price-reconciliation.md rule 2).

batches.notes: Batch 6: ten Priority A rental problem and season pages, each through writer, independent verifier, fixer and delta verifier. Words 4,352 -> 19,705. No title, H1, slug, permalink or canonical change. Three descriptions changed with a recorded reason. feels-wrong: the old one said "ride it straight back" for soft brakes, which contradicted the page's own stop-and-call list. breakdown: the old one stated a shop-pays policy that docs/OWNER-FACTS.md does not publish. fuel-what-petrol: "RON95 vs other grades" became E10 RON 95-III or E5 RON 92 (MoIT pages of 28 May and 22 Oct 2026, Government Portal of 1 Jun 2026). Removed or reworded originals, by article. feels-wrong (7): stop-now and report-soon wording rebuilt as checklists; the equipment-fine claim (no source); the maintenance split restated in OWNER-FACTS wording ("may include"); "the shop would rather see a healthy bike for nothing" and the gearbox line (implied policy). breakdown (6): the zero-skill fixes rebuilt against the Wave Alpha and Vision manuals (fuel valve ON/OFF only on the Wave Alpha, no RES); the renter-side list in OWNER-FACTS wording; "renting beats owning", the same-day replacement promise and the "day ten tow" line (unsourced). outside-hanoi (6): "no general law forbidding it" and the expressway fine claim replaced by Law 36/2024/QH15 Art. 25(3); "150 km is three to four hours" (unsourced); the documents list restated with 57(8)(b) and the handover wording; the roadside-mechanic pattern (unsourced). fuel-what-petrol (8): RON95 as the standard grade and "designed around RON95" replaced by the manuals (RON 91+ for the Vietnam-type Wave Alpha, ethanol up to 10%) and the MoIT grades; station density, rush-hour and consumption figures and "fuel costs less than a day's rental" (unsourced). couple (6): the passenger rule restated from Art. 33 (one person, two only in the listed cases); "rentals include helmets" turned into a handover question; the pillion technique list reworded. what-to-carry (4): the documents line restated with 57(8)(b) and 57(6)(b); the under-seat capacity claim (no manual figure); "many rentals have no USB socket" and "rentals normally include a helmet" (unsourced). complete-beginner (3): the licence rule restated with the moped class of Art. 34(1)(g) and 59(1)(a); the progression and the two beginner additions reworded. tet-holidays (7): shops closing for several days, "Hanoi empties dramatically", temple parking at its annual peak and the holiday-wave paragraph (unsourced; the week is now framed as a planning assumption); Tet 2027 dates from the Government Portal report of 22 Oct 2026 on notice 11483/TB-BNV. rainy-season (4): "afternoon storms, sudden, heavy, short", "mornings are usually dry" and "multi-day drizzle is the exception" replaced by the WMO 1991-2020 Hanoi table and the ADB/World Bank climate risk profile; the gear line reworded. winter (5): season, air-quality, cold-tyre and upside passages restated against the WMO table and the Wave Alpha manual choke bands; the one-line closing. Owner findings in other guides are listed in the progress log.

batches.notes: Batch 8: three Honda/Yamaha model comparisons and seven long-term rental pages, each through writer, independent verifier, fixer and delta verifier. No title, H1, slug, permalink or canonical change. batches.notes: Batch 10: the licence, IDP and moped cluster (3,611 -> 22,680 words), each through writer, independent verifier, fixer and delta verifier (1968-vienna-convention: the verifier's own edited copy adopted as the fix round, then delta-verified; small delta findings on idp-rules, moped, 50cc, expat, foreigners-50cc and which-countries applied by the lead). No title, H1, slug, permalink or canonical change. Five descriptions changed with a recorded reason: foreign-licence-exchange (the old one cited Circular 12/2025/TT-BCA and a three-month condition; Circular 108/2026/TT-BCA Article 24(1)(a) asks for a visa or temporary residence card of 90 days or more, or a permanent residence card), a1-licence ("valid to 175cc" for "below 175cc", Law 36 Article 89(2)(a)), expat (Circular 12/2025 and "3+ months"), learner-permit (cited Circular 14/2025/TT-BXD "since 1 September 2025" as current and "requires a licensed training course"; Circular 17/2026/TT-BXD amends it and Law Article 60(2) allows other forms of training), which-countries ("Only" and Article 57(8) as the recognition clause; recognition is 57(6)(b)). Corrections to verified pages: long-term-rider-licence-checklist-hanoi (batch 9) read Circular 108 Article 24(3)(d) as "issued in 1 day"; foreign-licence-exchange and idp-rules called exchange optional (Article 18(7)(a): a foreigner who needs to drive and holds a national licence must exchange, unless a treaty provides otherwise); idp-rules stated the 1949 permit point flatly (57(6)(d) names no treaty); links to the no-licence fine guide now say its figures follow the 2024 decree text. Removed or reworded originals, by article. foreign-licence-exchange (6): Circular 12/2025 as current (twice), the three-month residence condition, the old dossier list, the 2024 fine bands, the checkpoint exposure line. a1-licence (2): the summary list (now with the 125 cm3 / 11 kW limits as written) and the 2024 fine bands. idp-rules (4): Article 57(8) as the recognition clause, the 2024 fine band, the old exchange sentence ("without a new driving test" under Circular 12/2025), the dated "Verified against" line. what-is-a-moped (6): the lead definition (now quoted from Article 34(1)(g)), "miss one and it is something else" (the electric and petrol limbs are alternatives), the helmet fine, "40 km/h wherever it rides" (Circular 38/2024 Article 7 applies where no sign is posted, Article 4(2)), the 10-14 million band, the tuned-machine sentence. 50cc-licence (5): "basic vehicle-handling skills" (Article 56(4): the skill to control the vehicle), the 400,000-600,000 VND fine, the electric limb without the 50 km/h condition, "helmet rules" (Article 31(3) also covers motorised pedal bicycles), "insurance or IDP issues". 1968-vienna-convention (3): Vietnam's accession date now from the UN record (20 August 2014), the 1977 / non-party sentence (91 parties; China dropped, no row), Article 57(8) as the recognition clause. expat (6): Circular 12/2025, three months (twice), "no expiry", the district-of-registration processing claim, "the exchange does not require the theory test for most valid licences". foreigners-50cc (3): the legal-position lead ("basic handling skills"), "does not look good in that file" (unsourced), the fine schedule. learner-permit (2): "4 practical" hours (Circular 17/2026: class A 20 + 12), the 2-4 million band. which-countries (4): "makes its own 1968-format IDPs acceptable" (Circular 108 Article 30(1)), "the permit document itself" check, "1949 ... not recognised ... only the 1968 format", the document-carriage fine line. Sources read 2026-10-27/28: Law 36/2024/QH15 consolidated text 55/VBHN-VPQH (Articles 31, 33, 34, 56, 57, 59, 60, 61, 80, 89), Circular 108/2026/TT-BCA (Articles 4, 15, 16, 18(7), 24, 27-30, 41, Appendices I and XII), Circular 38/2024/TT-BGTVT Official Gazette text (Articles 4(2), 7), Circular 17/2026/TT-BXD (training hours; read via the Government document file), Civil Code 91/2015/QH13 Articles 584-585, the Decree 238/2026/NĐ-CP Official Gazette record, the UN Treaty Collection status of the 1968 Convention on Road Traffic (status as at 27 October 2026). Lint-protected original sources kept: the dead UN path on 1968-vienna-convention, Law Articles "58, 59" on foreigners-50cc, the Thanh Niên first-issue hours on learner-permit (owner findings).
